**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-24**

- **Member:** Skyler Ellison
- **Member ID:** W240749705
- **Reference number:** POC-1C51E72E1E-65750
- **Service denied:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
- **Plan:** PacificSource Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), Idaho
- **Governing policy:** *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* — https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the lower back disc surgery (decompression, CPT 63030) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated 2026-08-24 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-20, which is within 180 days of the date of the notice. I am submitting it together with the Member Appeal Form and supporting records. I may also submit through InTouch ("Ask a Question"), by email to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com, or by fax to 541-225-3628. The member services number listed for questions is 888-977-9299 (TTY 711).

Below I set out the plan's own published criteria and the matching entries in my medical record. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me.

---

### 1. The plan's criteria on conservative management

The guideline states:

> "Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management (Physical therapy optional)"

and:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

**What my records show:** I completed supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition to physical therapy, I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30 that gave me only about 3 weeks of partial relief. That is physical therapy plus more than one additional conservative treatment strategy, over a period longer than the six weeks the policy names.

The guideline also states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

**What my records show:** I completed the full course of physical therapy through discharge on 2026-07-03. My symptoms have been progressive over 12 months and are not relieved by rest; the injection relief lasted about 3 weeks and did not hold; the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief. Surgery is the more invasive therapy now under consideration, which is why this authorization was requested.

And:

> "Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

**What my records show:** 24 completed visits across the 10-week course, with a discharge note, documents my compliance with the therapy plan.

---

### 2. The plan's criteria on imaging

The guideline states:

> "Documentation of nerve root compression or thecal sac impingement on MRI or other advanced imaging performed within the past 9 months that correlates with clinical findings"

**What my records show:** An MRI of the lumbar spine performed on 2026-07-28 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. That is nerve root compression on MRI, and the study was performed within nine months of the request.

The guideline also states:

> "Imaging studies – All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

**What my records show:** The MRI findings are on the right side at L4-L5, and my symptoms and exam are on the same side and level: radicular pain into my right calf, positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The imaging and the clinical picture point to the same nerve root. I am enclosing the full radiology report. [Name of interpreting radiologist and imaging facility, from the MRI report]

---

### 3. The plan's criteria on radicular pain and functional impairment

The guideline states:

> "Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list. A separate passage of the guideline reads:

> "Nerve root tension sign Dermatomal sensory loss Motor strength deficit (myotomal) Abnormal reflex changes"

**What my records show:** I have radicular pain going into my right calf. My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

The guideline further states:

> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

**What my records show:** My pain has been progressive for 12 months and is not relieved by rest, and I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes. To complete this criterion precisely against the plan's own wording, I am asking my surgeon's office to supply the recorded pain intensity score and the specific activities affected: [documented pain rating out of 10, from office notes] and [specific ADLs/IADLs I am unable to perform, as documented].

The guideline also states:

> "All other reasonable sources of pain have been ruled out"

**What my records show:** The workup identified the L4-L5 disc extrusion with right lateral recess stenosis and L5 nerve root compression as the source, matching my symptoms and exam. [Any additional differential diagnoses considered and excluded, per the surgeon's notes]

---

### 4. About the "incomplete documentation" reason

The notice does not identify which required component of the documentation was found to be missing. The guideline states:

> "Documentation supporting medical necessity and a clearly stated plan of care should be submitted at the time of the request and must include the following components:"

That sentence ends in a colon and introduces a list of components that I do not have in front of me. If any specific component on that list was considered absent, I am asking the plan to identify it by name in its response so that it can be supplied. The records summarized above — the physical therapy discharge note, the medication and injection history, the 2026-07-28 MRI report, and my surgeon's examination findings — address duration of symptoms, conservative care and its failure, imaging, and correlating clinical findings.

I am not relying on the guideline's provisions for acute neurologic deterioration, cauda equina syndrome, or waiver of the conservative management requirement, because I completed a course of conservative care well beyond the six weeks the policy names.

Finally, I want to note plainly what I have and have not quoted: every passage in quotation marks above is taken word for word from the *Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery*. The excerpts I was able to obtain are the only policy language I have quoted. The guideline lists further conditions and components that are not reproduced here, and I am asking the plan to identify the specific criteria it applied in reaching this determination.

---

### What I am asking for

I respectfully ask PacificSource to:

1. Overturn the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030 and approve the requested procedure;
2. If the denial is maintained, tell me in writing exactly which documentation component from the guideline was found missing and which criterion was not met, so it can be addressed; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with training in spine surgery.

Enclosed with this letter: Member Appeal Form; MRI lumbar spine report dated 2026-07-28; physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03; medication and injection records; and my surgeon's office notes. [List any additional enclosures]

Thank you for taking another look at this. I am available at the phone number above if anything further is needed.

Sincerely,

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
**Skyler Ellison**

For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs.

Imaging studies – All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure.
Radicular pain (radiculitis/radiculopathy) with significant functional impairment or physical exam findings that correlate with radiculopathy or nerve root compression such as:
Nerve root tension sign Dermatomal sensory loss Motor strength deficit (myotomal) Abnormal reflex changes
Progressive or severe neurologic deficits secondary to cauda equina, lateral recess or foraminal compression (conservative management requirement waived)

The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present, and urgent intervention is indicated
